CF.horizon: n/a (rejected); would revisit as WATCH on a pullback toward mid-cycle valuation (~$85-95/share) or evidence the nitrogen supply loss is becoming structural rather than reversible
kill_criteria: De-escalation of the Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz reopening -> >25% pullback in benchmark urea/UAN prices within two quarters
Two consecutive quarters of GAAP operating margin below 30% (reverting toward the 24% ten-year median)
Yazoo City restart slips again past H1 2027, or investigation yields a materially larger fine/permanent capacity loss
Global nitrogen capacity additions (Blue Point, Dangote, others) outpace ~1.5%/yr demand growth
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 GAAP operating margin 50.5% is ABOVE the prior all-time-peak quarter (2022); 10-year median margin is ~24% - textbook low-P/E-at-peak setup (trailing P/E 8.67x)

Management explicitly attributes the spike to the Iran conflict / Strait of Hormuz disruption curtailing 50-60% of Middle East ammonia/urea capacity at points in 2026 - a named, live, geopolitical (likely transient) shock, not a structural change
Street is cutting FY2026 EPS estimates in real time even as the quarter beat: consensus fell from $17.61 (90d ago) to $15.10 (now), 6 down vs 0 up revisions in the last 30 days

Yazoo City ammonia release/explosion (2025-11-05) forced a town-wide shelter-in-place order; restart guidance slipped from 'Q4 2026 at earliest' (May 2026) to 'H1 2027' (Aug 2026); cumulative impairments ~$48M plus a separate unrelated $51M Donaldsonville electrolyzer impairment; active plaintiffs'-bar solicitation suggests pending toxic-tort litigation exposure
Quarterly dividend raised 20% (to $0.60/share) in July 2026, and buybacks were aggressive in H1 2026 - both declared right at what this dossier finds is a cyclical peak
H1 2026 GAAP EPS embeds ~$265M of pre-tax one-off gains (litigation settlement $170M, insurance recoveries, 45Q credits) on top of an already-elevated cyclical base
data_conflicts: None material found versus SEC filings for CF's core financials; d4/pipeline NTM and revision figures were used only as cross-checks and were consistent with the primary-source picture

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Multiple independent, primary-sourced lines of evidence (10+ year margin history, real-time analyst downgrades, management's own named transient catalyst, external forecaster consensus on 2027 normalisation) all point the same direction; main uncertainty is timing of the reversal, not its direction.

MPC.horizon: 12-24 months; revisit sizing after Q3 2026 results
kill_criteria: Q3 2026 refining & marketing margin (release ~3 Nov 2026) below $22/bbl while the share price is still above $350 (the price needs a sustained $20-22 margin; re-underwrite)
FY2026 actual EPS below ~$35 against the $55.73 consensus
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA above ~3.5x on a normalised (non-spike) EBITDA base
MPLX distribution growth (12.5% guided for 2026-27) is cut or its adjusted EBITDA becomes materially more volatile
A second consecutive quarter of guidance cuts (operating cost per barrel rising or throughput guided down without a stated turnaround reason)
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 refining margin $36.33/bbl is >2x the Q1 2026 and full-2025 run-rate ($16-18/bbl), jumped simultaneously across all three regions - a broad macro shock (very likely the same Iran-conflict disruption inflating CF's nitrogen margins), not company-specific improvement
Buying both CF and MPC together is a correlated bet on the same transient geopolitical driver, not two independent theses - a portfolio-construction concentration point for the lead

H1 2026 actual GAAP EPS ($19.46) implies the FY2026 consensus of $55.73 needs an H2 2026 acceleration BEYOND Q2's blowout print to be realised; 90-day estimate revisions show analysts chasing the print upward in real time (pipeline's own ntm_flags notes 'extreme dispersion') rather than a converged view - the 'cheap' 7.96x NTM P/E may not be reliable
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA has risen from ~0.7x (FY2022) to an estimated ~2.5x (FY2025) through the trough years
Capital return was cut hardest in 2025 (buybacks fell to $3.5B from $11.9B in 2022) and re-accelerated in 2026 exactly as margins spiked - the opposite of disciplined counter-cyclical buying

RA13 (6 Oct 2026): at $393.52 the price needs a sustained R&M margin of $19.7-21.1/bbl for ten years (cost of equity 7.95-9.0%); mid-cycle EPS at $17-20/bbl is about $14-21 so the stock trades at 19-28x mid-cycle earnings, not the 8x NTM headline

data_conflicts: Pipeline TTM revenue ($77.4B) vs COGS ($134.4B) implies a negative $57B gross profit - a clear pipeline data error; actual FY2025 revenue was $132.7B and this dossier's own TTM estimate is ~$153.6B per SEC XBRL/10-K

Pipeline 'actual/yago' EPS fields for MPC (FY2025 = $10.70) are Marathon's ADJUSTED (non-GAAP) EPS, not GAAP ($13.22 per the 10-K/earnings release) - unlabelled in the pipeline, which risks exactly the GAAP/adjusted mixing the prior audit (lead_v3_audit.md) flagged

Pipeline consolidated debt (~$5.4B) is far below the actual $32.8-32.9B (MPC $7.2B + MPLX $25.6B) as of Q2 2026; pipeline cash ($7.768B) DOES match exactly, so the error is specific to debt/revenue/COGS fields, not systemic

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Cash-flow arithmetic is primary-sourced (Q2 10-Q and release) and the conclusion is robust across cost of equity 7.95-10%; the evidence-based base margin ($19/bbl) is a judgement and the Iran-conflict duration is unknowable, which is why the bull case exists.

MPC.thesis_one_line: Largest US refiner with a genuinely steadier MPLX midstream arm, but at $393.52 the price needs a sustained $20-22/bbl refining margin against a $13-19 mid-cycle band, so the Q2 2026 spike is already in the price.

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA13): V1 capitalised the TTM spike (EBIT $14.1bn, FCF $12.9bn, implied -11.2% a year at WACC 7.07%) and compared it with a consensus decline set by the same spike (in_line), used consolidated net debt with no MPLX noncontrolling interest, and did not deduct SBC. Rebuilt as an equity DCF on MPC-attributable free cash flow (OCF - capex - SBC - $813m H1 distributions to MPLX public unitholders) from the FY2025 mid-cycle anchor ($3.05bn at a $16.87/bbl margin; +$0.84bn per $1/bbl): at a $19/bbl base margin the $111.4bn market cap implies 4.6% a year at a 7.95% cost of equity and 7.1% at 9.0% against a base of about 3%; the price equals a 3%-growth cash flow only at a sustained $19.7-21.1/bbl margin. Implied above base; V1 verdict fair and base -17% a year are both consistent with this.

MPC.scenario_basis: Corrected 6 Oct 2026 (RA13). From $393.52 (25 Sep 2026), 3-year annualised, price plus $12 dividends plus about $18 a share for the retained H2 2026 windfall. EPS = (3.5bn normalised attributable net income + $0.84bn x (R&M margin - $16.87)) / shares, shares -4% a year from 283m. Bear: margin $15, 14x EPS $7.7. Base: margin $19, 13x EPS $21.1. Bull: Iran-conflict premium persists, margin $28, 10x EPS $51.3. Replaces V1 -49% / -17% / +45%.

This dossier could NOT independently confirm whether a 2026-2027 emissions 'pre-buy' is inflating current order activity - management's own commentary frames EPA clarity as unlocking deferred demand (constructive), but that is management's framing, not independently verified against neutral industry order/backlog data; Section 232 truck tariffs (effective ~Nov 2025) are an entangled second variable

Granular segment-level guidance (truck delivery counts, Parts margin range, FS pre-tax range) that the assignment brief expected was NOT found in the press-release exhibits reviewed - only industry-volume and capex/R&D guidance was available; the finer detail likely sits in the earnings-call transcript, which this pass could not access (FMP transcript tool required a higher plan tier)
